title: Muscle creatine levels and sprint performance in young adult vegans and vegetarians after 7 days of creatine monohydrate supplementation - PMC
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the hypothesis that creatine supplementation in a vegan and vegetarian population would lead to an increase in TCr in skeletal muscle and an associated improvement in short‐term exercise performance. Surprisingly, the CM average baseline TCr level of 114 ± 17 mmol/kg in the present study resembles that previously reported for omnivores, and with supplementation, the VEG TCr content approached the level of an apparent muscle threshold (~160 mmol/kg) as determined in omnivores (Kreider et al., 2017). In the present study, there were no significant differences between groups when assessing measures of exercise performance: peak power, mean power, and concentration of capillary blood metabolites, despite the elevated muscle TCr level. Hence, there is a need for increased sample sizes and thereby adequately powered studies to facilitate stratification and analysis by diet group (vegan, vegetarian) and duration (i.e., 6 months, 5–10 years), to determine whether diet group or duration serves as mediating factors for muscle creatine and/or exercise performance.
